//: Mutation matrix for probe_musicqueue (multi-album music queues). Every mutant breaks ONE rule the queue builders or their action rows own and must turn the probe red; a SURVIVOR means the assertion guarding that rule is inert. The headline is `shuffle-only-within-a-record`: it produces a queue that is still a complete, still a random-looking permutation, and is exactly the wrong thing — records stay contiguous, so the queue never crosses one and crossfade goes back to never firing. Driven by native/tools/mutate.py (never a hand-rolled loop; see CONTRIBUTING).

mutants.name: shuffle-only-within-a-record
mutants.//: THE headline mutant, and the only one that is subtle. It still returns a permutation containing every track exactly once, so a completeness check passes it — but each track can only land inside the run of entries from its own album, so every record stays contiguous and the queue never produces a cross-record boundary. That is the single thing this whole feature exists to produce. Killed by the album-RUNS assertion and by the crossfade section, which then finds nothing to fade.
mutants.replace:
int lo = i; while (lo > 0 && q[lo - 1].albumKey == q[i].albumKey) --lo;
        const int j = lo + int(rng.bounded(quint32(i - lo + 1)));

mutants.name: shuffle-does-nothing
mutants.//: The degenerate failure: 'Shuffle all' hands back the ordered queue. Killed by the assertion that the shuffled order differs from the input at all.

mutants.name: shuffle-assigns-instead-of-swapping
mutants.//: The classic Fisher-Yates bug: overwrite rather than exchange, and the queue silently duplicates some tracks and loses others. The size is unchanged, so only a MULTISET check catches it.

mutants.name: shuffle-ignores-the-seed
mutants.//: The seed is a parameter so the shuffle has no hidden input and a probe can pin a permutation. Ignoring it makes every queue in a session identical, which is the one thing a shuffle must not be.

mutants.name: artist-play-all-plays-only-the-first-album
mutants.//: The exact behaviour this feature replaces: a queue that stops at one record. Killed by the full expected title list for the artist.
mutants.find: for (const MusicLibrary::Album& b : a->albums) appendAlbum(b, out);

mutants.name: artist-play-all-reverses-the-discography
mutants.//: Album order is the index's (year, then title) and is restated nowhere. Reversing it still yields every track exactly once, so only the ORDER assertion discriminates.
mutants.find: for (const MusicLibrary::Album& b : a->albums) appendAlbum(b, out);
mutants.replace: for (int i = a->albums.size() - 1; i >= 0; --i) appendAlbum(a->albums[i], out);

mutants.name: stale-artist-key-plays-the-whole-library
mutants.//: A row naming an artist the rescan dropped must build NOTHING. Falling back to everything means a stale route silently starts an hour of the wrong music.
mutants.find: if (!a) return out;                 // stale route: empty, never "some other artist"

mutants.name: library-queue-stops-at-the-first-artist
mutants.//: "Shuffle all music" that is really "shuffle the first artist". Killed by the track count and the full expected order.

mutants.name: entry-forgets-which-record-it-is-from
mutants.//: albumKey is what the now-playing page re-reads the sleeve from at each boundary, and what makes 'did the shuffle break the records apart' answerable at all. Losing it is invisible to a title-order check.

mutants.name: entry-carries-the-album-artist-instead-of-the-track-artist
mutants.//: On a compilation every track has its own artist, and a library-wide shuffle's queue row says 'title — artist'. Taking the album artist labels every compilation track 'Various Artists'.

mutants.name: drop-the-shuffle-all-music-row
mutants.//: The verb is only reachable because the row exists — there is no other surface on the themed layout that could offer it. Without the row the whole feature is dead code.

mutants.name: shuffle-all-music-row-on-a-one-track-library
mutants.//: A library with one track has nothing to shuffle; offering it is a row that does the same thing as the track under it.

mutants.name: drop-the-artist-verb-rows
mutants.//: Same as above one level down: without these two rows an artist's discography can only be played one album at a time, which is the gap being filled.

mutants.name: artist-verb-rows-on-a-one-track-artist
mutants.//: Withholding them is a deliberate absence, so it needs its own tripwire: a one-track artist must show its album row and nothing else.

mutants.name: play-all-row-carries-the-shuffle-type
mutants.//: The type is the ENTIRE routing contract for these rows (they have no url). A Play-all row typed as a shuffle plays the discography in random order while the label promises otherwise.

mutants.name: verb-rows-carry-a-url
mutants.//: A url on one of these rows sends it down the surface's generic 'this item is a file' route, which opens the KEY as a path instead of building a queue. The rows must stay url-less to be routed by type.

mutants.name: shuffle-all-music-row-carries-a-key
mutants.//: Keyless is what means 'the whole library' at the play site. Any key at all makes it look like an artist route, and musicKeyOf would hand that text to forArtist.
